root_causes.finding: A send began with about 12 ms left of its original 60 s budget. Delivery succeeded but ACK timed out; the unidentified unknown record permanently blocked later automatic sends.
root_causes.correction: Require a minimum send budget at each pre-transport boundary; reconcile a unique persisted live own echo only after independent protocol verification. Never resend an uncertain delivery.

root_causes.finding: After the approximately 08:40 host reboot, the account was waiting for QR login and OneBot port 6301 was unavailable.
root_causes.correction: User completed QR login. Boot-only readiness now accepts a fresh disconnected worker; normal health checks still require a connection.

root_causes.finding: Daily aggregation blocked the sequential heartbeat and synchronous I/O blocked the event loop; monitor overview repeatedly decoded and returned full runtime snapshots.
root_causes.correction: Single-flight background report finalization, drained worker I/O on shutdown, SQL aggregates, compact monitor samples, reusable CPU measurement baselines.

test_groups.scope: runtime, daily report, monitoring, report routes, diary, QQ deadline, supervisor, Linux readiness/deployment
QQ source, actor, private actor, status, launcher and resource monitoring

limitations: Activation still takes roughly 220 seconds while replaying durable state; this incident fix does not optimize startup replay.
The GUI model reply took about 51 seconds from receipt to delivery; interface responsiveness does not imply low model latency.
QQ continues to apply its original deadline and newer-context protection. Cumulative failed counts include superseded events and are not sufficient to diagnose a persistent outage.
Provider cache hit tokens were observed in live QQ traces, but no controlled cache-hit-ratio benchmark was performed.
